speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is happening inside, tell me: when did these symptoms first start, and does your belly look like it has sausage-shaped ridges when you touch it?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

The clinical picture of an 8-month-old with feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, worsening pain on palpation (crying), and a history of being fussy is highly suggestive of intussusception. Given the high suspicion for a surgical emergency, please confirm if there has been any vomiting or blood in the stool, and proceed immediately to an ultrasound examination.
